subject.title: Discord account-to-agent routing falls back to default agent instead of matching by account name

question: Should Discord multi-account routing add a guarded same-name accountId-to-agent fallback after explicit bindings miss, or should explicit bindings remain the only supported routing contract?
rationale: The source-level behavior and permission concern are clear, but changing fallback selection affects route ownership, session state, model/provider context, and per-agent permission boundaries for existing Discord multi-account setups.

options.title: Approve guarded fallback
options.body: Route non-default Discord account IDs to an existing same-named configured agent only after explicit binding tiers miss, with diagnostics, docs, regression tests, and live Discord proof.

options.title: Keep explicit bindings only
options.body: Leave runtime routing unchanged and add docs, doctor, or status warnings for Discord accounts that appear intended to bind to same-named agents.

options.title: Use prior PR as source material
options.body: Treat the closed PR implementation as a sketch, but require conflict resolution, phantom-agent guards, distinct match diagnostics, and real Discord proof before any replacement lands.

recommendation.title: Approve guarded fallback
recommendation.body: Route non-default Discord account IDs to an existing same-named configured agent only after explicit binding tiers miss, with diagnostics, docs, regression tests, and live Discord proof.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest history signal across shared routing, route/session policy, and permission-sensitive routing decisions.
